title: The GTM Platform internal design system
author: Amal Irgashev
howToUse: Grep `search` for the job you are doing before writing any component.
Read `rules` for the chosen entry; those are decisions, not suggestions.
Signatures are in agent/props.json, keyed by component, or in the rules file.
Read `source` last, for props. Never copy a component into the consumer repo.
No entry fits a product question? That is a design decision. Surface it, do not invent it.

entries.name: agent-thread-rail
entries.summary: In focus mode this rail replaces the navigation rail — it is not a third sidebar. Width follows AppShell's rail (246–400px, default 246).
entries.note: Focus-mode rail (CORE 05/12): agent feature destinations (SidebarNav), then list chrome (optional SearchInput + one Display menu), then collapsible grouped threads. Thread management via DropdownMenu — no private chrome, no Status/Project tabs, no standalone New thread button.

entries.name: agent-thread
entries.summary: The thread measure is 704px — a documented contentWidth exception, not a fifth rung (`APP_SHELL_RULES`). Centre it in the work pane. The number lives in one place, `--gtm-container-thread`, reached as `max-w-(--container-thread)`: an exc...
entries.note: CORE 05/12 conversation column: 704px measure (documented exception), user right-aligned, agent content full-width, interpretation block with speech-tail radius, centred day dividers.

entries.name: app-rail-preview
entries.summary: Collapsed destination icons open one contextual HoverCard to the right after hover or focus intent. Expanded rows already carry their labels and do not duplicate the card.
entries.note: The collapsed product rail keeps destination recognition in the icon and restores context in one right-side HoverCard. The preview is a bounded summary of an existing server document, never a second product page.

entries.name: app-shell
entries.summary: The header is earned, not permanent. The sidebar already says where you are, so chrome above the content has to justify itself on every route rather than being inherited from the layout.
entries.note: The rules themselves are `APP_SHELL_RULES` below, not this comment. `/design` renders that array verbatim beside the live pattern, so the shell a builder reads in the gallery and the shell this file mounts are the same strings.

entries.name: capacity-metric
entries.summary: Capacity is a remaining allowance, not usage completed. The dominant number says what is left and the meter fills in the same direction.

entries.name: change-feed
entries.summary: ChangeFeed is the quieter Home band under the DecisionRow queue. It is observational — no Approve CTA, no action lane. Home is a router, so a row that can name a destination opens that surface on the whole row, the same verb Coming up uses.
entries.note: Home quieter band (CORE 01/13). Flat hairline rows — observational, no action lane, no Frame card. Containment ledger: the decision queue is a panel; this feed is a window onto something continuous.

entries.name: choice-cards
entries.summary: A fork is cards, not a radio list and not two forms stacked. Each card names the path and what it opens.
entries.note: A fork is a set of cards. The chosen card opens one section. Two forms in one view is the failure this pattern exists to prevent.

entries.name: coming-up-calendar
entries.summary: List is the default Coming up view. List / Calendar is a compact icon switch in the section header, replacing the meeting count. 3 days, week, and month are the same compact icon switch, calendar-only. There is no drag, create, recurrenc...
entries.note: Home's Coming up band. List is the default. List / Calendar is a compact icon switch in the section header, in the slot Paper used for the meeting count. 3 days / week / month use the same compact icon switch, calendar-only. Inspired by ReUI Event Calendar 1's range switch and Event Calendar 6's hover detail, drawn in CORE tokens. Not the ReUI engine: no drag, no create, no recurrence, no resource columns.

entries.name: confirmable-action
entries.summary: Required, not optional, for any action that permanently destroys something or sends on a rep's behalf: deleting a campaign, wiping account memory, releasing a queued send, revoking a rep's Gmail grant. If undo is impossible, the flow is...
entries.note: The rules themselves are `CONFIRMABLE_ACTION_RULES` below, not this comment. `/design` renders that array verbatim beside the live pattern, so the decision a builder reads in the gallery and the decision this file enforces are the same strings, and there is exactly one place to change either.

entries.name: conversation-row
entries.summary: An inbox row is not a QueueRow. It is a conversation rung with a 32px mark lane, contact over account, and a trailing column of meta over the status chip — never meta inside the identity and badge floating mid-row.
entries.note: Inbox agent-held conversation — carved out of QueueRow. Geometry: 32px mark lane, two-line identity (contact over account), trailing meta-over-badge column. Unread = weight + a corner badge on the ProviderMark (never a left gutter, never colour alone). The row is click-to-open. There is no overflow menu and no hover-revealed action.

entries.name: decision-row
entries.summary: Home is a router. The row's only verb is Open — never Approve, Send, or Snooze on the Home queue (platform decision 1.2). Owning surfaces hold the decision UX.
entries.note: Home ranked queue item — 48px conversation rung with source mark + rank reason. Decision 1.2: the row's only verb is Open. No action lane. CopyGrammar: Object → State → Evidence → Action → Receipt.

entries.name: diff-row
entries.summary: DiffRow shows one field mutation: caps label · before → after. The default is chips (muted line-through before, ink after). `layout="block"` is the same evidence for multiline markdown: stacked pre-wrapped mono blocks, never a second sid...
entries.note: Structured before→after evidence for its two consumers: a play version compared to live (VersionedEditor's diff slot) and a proposed or completed write (Receipt). ChangeSet is one quiet subcard; sections group related fields; DiffRow is one mutation as label + before chip → after chip. No Frame-in-Frame, no action lane, no sparklines.

entries.name: empty-state
entries.summary:
Compose `ui/empty` (Header → Media → Title → Description, optional Content). Never a bare centred `

` pretending to be an empty surface. Reference: ReUI `c-empty-*` under `web/reference/reui/empty/`.
entries.note: Zero-data surfaces get a quiet visual centre, not a lonely caption and not ambient motion. Composition follows the shadcn / ReUI Empty family (`ui/empty` — see `web/reference/reui/empty/` for pulled examples). Empty is settled: never Orb, never Spinner, never continuous decoration.

entries.summary: This is the explicit submit family: creation flows, invite flows, wizard steps. Nothing has happened until the user presses the button. If the surface is configuration, a set of independent switches a user comes back to and adjusts, it i...

entries.name: input-request
entries.summary: Use InputRequest only to collect missing information. ApprovalArtifact remains the boundary for a consequential send or write.
entries.note: The Agent supplies a bounded semantic request. The host owns identity, lifecycle and presentation selection. Surface adapters own pixels.

entries.name: metric-card
entries.summary: Dashboard headline metrics are cards with an icon, a clear title, one dominant value, and one context line. Dense record metadata remains a StatReadout row or cell.
entries.note: The drill trigger covers the card and is a sibling of the info button rather than its ancestor. A role on the panel would read as one control to assistive technology and take the provenance trigger out of the accessibility tree with it, which no amount of event handling repairs.

entries.name: onboarding-dialog
entries.summary: OnboardingDialog teaches a surface. WizardDialog remains the create flow. Do not put fields in this dialog.
entries.note: The rules themselves are `ONBOARDING_DIALOG_RULES` below, not this comment. /design renders that array verbatim beside the live pattern.

entries.name: overflow-tabs
entries.summary: Fit tabs that fit; park the rest under Other + Popover. Never a horizontal ScrollArea on a tab strip — especially not inside a narrow list sidebar.
entries.note: Narrow rails (Inbox list sidebar at 384 / 320) cannot afford a horizontal ScrollArea on a status tab strip — a track + gutter in the one pane that least can spend width. The established pattern (ServiceNow Horizon, Nuxt UI collapse, CSS-Tricks adapting tabs) is: fit what you can, park the rest under Other + Popover. Never wrap TabsList in overflow-x scroll.

entries.name: page-band
entries.summary: Chrome may only assert what the content cannot: where you are (the sidebar), how deep you are (a lineage band), what you can do (the page toolbar). Zero, one, or one. Never two.
entries.note: The rules themselves are `PAGE_BAND_RULES` below, not this comment. `/design` renders that array verbatim beside the live pattern, so the band a builder reads in the gallery and the band this file draws are the same strings.

entries.name: page-frame
entries.summary: A page is one readable column, 768px wide, centred in whatever the shell gives it. That is `max-w-3xl` off the stock scale, chosen because it is the widest step where a label and description on the left and their control on the right sti...
entries.note: The rules themselves are `PAGE_FRAME_RULES` below, not this comment. `/design` renders that array verbatim beside the live pattern, so the shape a builder reads in the gallery and the shape this file imposes are the same strings.

entries.name: page-masthead
entries.summary: A masthead is content, not chrome. It states what today is and what is in it; PageBand states where you are and what you can do. That is why Home mounts a masthead and no band, and why a surface that already carries a lineage band does n...
entries.note: The rules themselves are `PAGE_MASTHEAD_RULES` below, not this comment. `/design` renders that array verbatim beside the live pattern.

entries.name: posture-control
entries.summary: The sanctioned agent toggle is this segmented Tabs control in the sidebar. A floating duplicate in a global header is forbidden (`APP_SHELL_RULES`).
entries.note: Segmented Home / Agent switch — every Core 5 surface board. Decision: `surface-decisions-2026-08-10.md` §2. Implemented with the Tabs primitive (same segmented family as ToggleGroup). ⌘J still toggles Agent.

entries.name: provider-action
entries.summary: A provider hop is a compact outline control with the shipped ProviderLogo and a verb. Do not draw a second local Salesforce or LinkedIn button.
entries.note: An outbound provider hop is a compact outline control with that provider's logo and a verb. Alerts, Accounts peeks, and Inbox use this instead of a second button-plus-icon local. The href is a server https URL. The browser never invents one from an id.

entries.name: provider-mark
entries.summary: Provider identity is a real brand mark in an IconWell, not an initial tile and not a bare SVG. Inbox rows, tool activity, receipts, and thread-rail HoverCard previews name the channel with this module. The thread-rail row itself does not...
entries.note: The rules themselves are `PROVIDER_MARK_RULES` below, not this comment. Second sanctioned brand module beside `ui/logo.tsx`. Always native brand colour inside `IconWell` — never mono, never a bare logo (`surface-decisions` §5, updated 2026-08-10).

entries.name: queue-row
entries.summary: Lanes are fixed-width so the columns line up down the queue: 16px checkbox, 10px state dot, the flexible identity, 110px badge, 100px meta, 28px action. A lane that sizes itself to its contents makes every row a different shape, and a re...
entries.note: The rules themselves are `QUEUE_ROW_RULES` below, not this comment. `/design` renders that array verbatim beside the live pattern, so the row a builder reads in the gallery and the row this file draws are the same strings.

entries.name: receipt
entries.summary: Receipt is the terminal step of CopyGrammar: Object → State → Evidence → Action → Receipt. Render inline under the action and keep it inspectable.
entries.note: Artifact-tier confirmation after a decision (CopyGrammar terminal). Stacked Frame like ApprovalArtifact: chrome header → optional figure → body (ChangeSet). An optional 24px mark names the result family without adding another row. Title leads; figure is label-scale mono only here. Diff evidence is a quiet ChangeSet subcard — never Frame-in-Frame.

entries.name: record-header
entries.summary: RecordHeader is object identity inside the work pane — title, status, and quiet meta. It is not a PageBand and must not host a second band of filters.
entries.note: Shared Accounts + Campaigns object chrome (CORE 03/04): identity, status, quiet meta — not a second PageBand. Title leads; supporting lines sit on a real gap, not gap-none + mt hacks.

entries.name: review-band
entries.summary: A review band presents one object to act on. It is not a list row, not a New-this-week card, and not a contained PageSection. Suggested play is a titled flat section; this band is the object inside it (`PAGE_SECTION_RULES`).
entries.note: The rules themselves are `REVIEW_BAND_RULES` below, not this comment. `/design` renders that array verbatim beside the live pattern.

entries.name: schema-cell
entries.summary: A cell has a schema type, and the type picks the chrome. Surfaces do not restyle the same field two ways.
entries.note: The rules themselves are `SCHEMA_CELL_RULES` below, not this comment. `/design` renders that array verbatim beside the live pattern.

entries.name: setting-section
entries.summary: A row is one setting: a label, at most a one line description beneath it, and exactly ONE control opposite. Two controls in a lane are two settings that have not been split yet, and a description that needs a second line is a section, no...
entries.note: The rules themselves are `SETTING_RULES` below, not this comment. `/design` renders that array verbatim beside the live pattern, so the anatomy a builder reads in the gallery and the anatomy this file imposes are the same strings.

entries.name: sidebar-nav
entries.summary: Selection is a fill, ink and weight. Never a border, never a shadow, never a left bar. A selected row is the same height in the same place with `bg-selected` behind it, at `text-ink` on the medium step, so the rail does not reflow and no...
entries.note: The rules themselves are `SIDEBAR_NAV_RULES` below, not this comment. `/design` renders that array verbatim beside the live pattern, so the nav a builder reads in the gallery and the nav this file draws are the same strings.

entries.summary: Rules for sidebar trees, shared by the Agent rail and memory browser. Agent folder headings use their identity icon; sections use a trailing chevron. File directories use sentence-case rows, folder icons, a trailing disclosure chevron an...

entries.name: site-mark
entries.summary: - A link to an external site wears that site's favicon at the data rung, and nothing else. No provider wordmark, no coloured chip, no letter avatar. - The mark degrades in one direction only: favicon, then the globe glyph. A broken image...

entries.name: split-view
entries.summary: Panes have roles, not sides. One is the work pane, where the decision happens; the other is either the reference pane (facts the decision is made against) or the list pane (the triage sidebar that picks which decision is on screen). Nami...
entries.note: The rules themselves are `SPLIT_VIEW_RULES` below, not this comment. `/design` renders that array verbatim beside the live pattern, so the split a builder reads in the gallery and the split this file lays out are the same strings.

entries.name: stat-readout
entries.summary: StatReadout is the dense number pattern for record chrome, metadata columns, and compact run summaries. Six settled boards put those values in a label/value pair at 28, 40, or 66px.
entries.note: The rules themselves are `STAT_READOUT_RULES` below, not this comment. `/design` renders that array verbatim beside the live pattern.

entries.name: state-notice
entries.summary: This is the one shape for a thing that did not happen: a send the door refused, a job that stopped, a connection that lapsed, an import that found nothing to do. Never invent a second one per surface.
entries.note: The rules themselves are `STATE_NOTICE_RULES` below, not this comment.

entries.name: table-filters
entries.summary: This popover writes request state. It never filters mounted rows. The table renders the page the server returned for the current values.
entries.note: The rules themselves are `TABLE_FILTERS_RULES` below, not this comment. `/design` renders FilterableTable's rules; this file is the Filters popover that composition owns. Copy the ReUI Filters command shape (c-filters-3 custom trigger, hierarchical category drill-in), re-expressed in CORE 14.

entries.name: versioned-editor
entries.summary: VersionedEditor is the third save family. Prompt changes stay browser-local until Save draft updates the one mutable team draft or Publish creates the immutable version. Local, Saving draft, Draft saved, Publishing, and Publish failed be...
entries.note: Rules for VersionedEditor + PublishGate.

entries.name: wizard-dialog
entries.summary: Use one Dialog, one scroll body, and one footer. A branch changes the current step; it never opens a second dialog.
entries.note: WizardDialog is the one in-product create flow: a compact progress trail, one scroll body, and one footer whose primary names the next commitment.
